answer:
Perform a variable-cell relaxation (vc-relax) of BiFeO3 in the R3c (space group 161) ferroelectric phase, followed by a single-point SCF calculation on the relaxed structure to obtain the final total energy.
The starting structure is a 10-atom (2 formula unit) R3c BiFeO3 cell in the hexagonal setting with lattice parameters a = 5.59 Å and c = 4.62 Å, with atomic positions generated from the standard R3c Wyckoff positions (Bi at 2a, Fe at 2a, O at 6b).
Use LDA pseudopotentials from PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard: bi.upf, fe.upf, and o.upf.
Set the exchange-correlation functional to LDA (PW parametrization).
Set ecutwfc = 60 Ry and ecutrho = 360 Ry.
Set etot_conv_thr = 1.0e-8, forc_conv_thr = 1.0e-7, and conv_thr = 1.0e-8.
Use a Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid of 3 x 3 x 1 with a half shift (offset 1 1 1).
Set ibrav = 6 (hexagonal) for the cell symmetry.
Run the vc-relax calculation allowing full relaxation of all nine components of the cell matrix and all atomic positions.
After the vc-relax converges, extract the relaxed cell vectors and atomic coordinates.
Run an SCF calculation on the relaxed structure using identical ecutwfc, ecutrho, k-point grid, functional, and pseudopotentials.
Report the fully relaxed atomic structure (cell vectors and Cartesian or fractional coordinates of all 10 atoms) and the final SCF total energy in Ry.
